$comment: The Explore canon. Every preset is also a worked example of the Build grammar, so each must be expressible as {dataset, measure, dimension, period, filters}. If a preset cannot be expressed in the builder vocabulary, either extend the vocabulary or drop the preset. A chart whose dataset has a definition in dimensions.json renders that definition.
evergreen_test: Would this chart still be worth showing in 2035? If the title names a specific scheme, brand or year, it fails and belongs in the events layer instead.

$status.$comment: Every preset carries a status, so the gap between the canon and what the cube can serve is visible rather than discovered chart by chart. The UI renders anything not live as a 'coming when X lands' entry, and cross-checks the authored status against what the cube actually resolves: a disagreement is shown as a warning, because a stale status is worse than none.
$status.live: Renders from the cube as built.
$status.blocked: Correctly specified. Waiting on a deliverable named in requires.
$status.invalid: The preset's own configuration is wrong. requires names the fix.
$status.precedence: status is the worst outstanding state; requires lists every outstanding item, not just the worst.
$status.on_unblocking: When a dataset a preset waits on lands, re-run the triage before building the chart. The canon was written well ahead of the data, so some blocked presets will want rewriting rather than unblocking.

$note_templates.$comment: A note that states a figure must be templated from the build, or it drifts the moment the data moves. note_template resolves {dotted.path} against the manifest, the preset's dataset entry in it, and the preset's measure and dimension definitions; |pct formats a proportion. A plain note may not contain a figure at all: the UI flags one that does.

$composite.$comment: A deliberate, closed exception to one-chart-one-question, for the two questions that only exist as a comparison of two series. Not a sixth shape: both render through the trend renderer. Composite presets are never offered in the builder, and the UI flags them as a curated comparison so a reader does not mistake them for something the grammar can express.

defaults.$comment: Chart-level defaults that are not per-preset decisions. mix_smoothing: monthly share on survivors data swings too hard to read, so a mix chart defaults to a trailing share and offers monthly as a toggle. top_n_basis: which window ranks the values that keep their own line; the rest become one remainder series.
defaults.$colour_slots_comment: The line palette has eight colours (src/lib/theme.ts: no set of colours keeps more lines apart under colour blindness). On a mix chart the first colour_slots_by_trailing go to the largest series over the trailing window, the rest by peak rolling share over the preset's period, and any series beyond the palette is drawn as a grey context line. 5 keeps every current contender on the owner_country chart in colour while leaving three slots for the categories that carried earlier decades.

mix_default_start.$comment: A mix chart over all time crushes its story into the right of the frame whenever the dimension spent decades with one category. The default start is the first month the dimension had something to show: at least min_categories categories above min_share, sustained for sustain_months, measured on the 12-month rolling mix so it does not move with monthly noise. All time stays available as a toggle and is never the default. Computed in the browser, like the rolling share and the suppression guards, so these numbers change without a rebuild.
mix_default_start.$threshold_note: min_share 0.005 puts powertrain at 2009-10, where hybrids first became visible; 0.02 puts it at 2018-07 and hides the nine-year ramp. Do not lower it below 0.004: at 0.003 powertrain falls back to 1938-01, because 1940s diesel sat near 0.36% and the now-extinct Other category near 0.71%. The qualifying run is 202 months and the nearest non-qualifying run is 5, so sustain_months is what rejects the mid-century near-misses.
mix_default_start.$cardinality_note: Only low-cardinality dimensions. The test measures diversity, and diversity saturates immediately when a dimension has hundreds of values: on make it returns whatever month the denominator floor allows and the composition clause never binds.

public_copy.$comment: Wording for visitors on the Explore page, where config/dimensions.json (frozen until the 8 November 2026 gate) carries text written for maintainers. Keyed by dataset or dimension id; anything not listed falls back to dimensions.json. After the gate each entry moves onto its dataset or dimension there (D-042).

dataset_definitions.registrations_surviving: Each month counts the vehicles first registered in New Zealand that month that are still registered on the snapshot date.
dataset_definitions.nz_new: Each month counts the vehicles first registered in New Zealand that month, new when they arrived, that are still registered on the snapshot date.
dataset_definitions.used_imports: Each month counts the vehicles first registered in New Zealand that month, previously registered overseas, that are still registered on the snapshot date.

dimension_notes.built_in: Where a vehicle was built is not recorded for almost every vehicle first registered before late 1985, and is recorded for almost all since. The grey line near the top of the chart until then is that gap in the record, not where vehicles came from.
dimension_notes.vehicle_year_band: Age on the snapshot date, not when the vehicle was bought. It is counted from the year NZTA records for each vehicle, not from when it was built: for a vehicle sold new here since 2007, the year it was first registered here; for a used import, a year from its life overseas, usually when it was built or first registered there. For vehicles sold new here before 2007 that year is less consistent, sometimes a year early. A year, not a date, so an age can be out by a year.
dimension_notes.age_at_registration_band: Age when first registered in New Zealand, counted from the year NZTA records for each vehicle. A vehicle sold new here since 2007 is 0 years old by definition, because that year is its first registration here; for a used import it is a year from its life overseas, usually when it was built or first registered there. For vehicles sold new here before 2007 that year is less consistent, sometimes a year early. A year, not a date, so an age can be out by a year. Counted among vehicles still registered at the snapshot: arrivals from earlier years have had longer to leave the register, and vehicles do not all leave at the same rate, so the longer the span, the more the ages shown may differ from those that arrived at the time.
dimension_notes.powertrain: NZTA does not record whether a hybrid is mild or full. Mild hybrids are picked out by model name, so the mild hybrid line counts only the ones identified; the note below says what share that is.

builder.$comment: The Build page: a sentence a visitor completes to draw one chart, through the same panel and resolver as Explore. A measure offers only the dimensions it lists here (each with the words the sentence uses for it), and of those only the ones that resolve and draw against the cube as built. Ids name what config/measures.json and config/dimensions.json define; the words are for visitors. not_offered tells the visitor what is missing and why (D-044).
builder.$period_by_shape_comment: A distribution sums its whole period, so all time would mix decades whose records differ (docs/MODEL_AND_AGE.md, before 2007). The time row still offers all time.
builder.$ranking_period_comment: The time row offers this period too wherever it makes the chart a league (a high-cardinality breakdown such as brand), so a visitor can rank the latest 12 months and switch back to the lines. Manufacturer group is medium cardinality in config/dimensions.json, so it stays a mix chart (D-045).

measures.$top_n_comment: The values that keep their own line on a mix chart; the rest become one remainder, All other. Reserved tokens (not recorded, no reference match) keep their own grey line and never join it (D-046). make and parent_group as brand-share uses. built_in is capped at 10 of its 46 values in the 2026-09 cube: its country is not recorded for almost every vehicle first registered before about 1986, and that gap shows as its own Not recorded line.
measures.note: Share, not volume. These are vehicles still registered at the snapshot, so older months are thinned by scrappage and a count would partly measure it. Share removes the shrinkage every group shares, but groups leave the register at different rates, so older months lean towards groups whose vehicles stay registered longer.

measures.note_template: The combined share of the {measure.top_n} largest in each month. Membership is recomputed monthly, so the line reflects concentration rather than the fortunes of a fixed set. A falling line means the largest hold less of the market: more may be competing, or the same ones may be sharing it more evenly. Vehicles with no match in the brand list count in the total but never take a place, which holds the line down in the early decades.

dimension_notes.$comment: What a canon preset says about a dimension in its own note, which a built chart would otherwise lose. Here rather than in public_copy.dimension_notes so Explore does not show it twice.
dimension_notes.segment: The register records most SUVs as station wagons, so they count as cars here.
dimension_notes.import_status: These are vehicles still registered at the snapshot, and new and used vehicles leave the register at different rates, so an older month's split may differ from what was bought at the time. In recent cohorts used imports leave faster, which understates their share; in some older cohorts it runs the other way.
dimension_notes.owner_country: Ownership is as at today, not at registration: every year shown counts each brand under the country that owns it now.
dimension_notes.parent_group: Group ownership is as at today, not at registration: every year shown counts each brand under the group that owns it now.

not_offered: Numbers of vehicles. These figures count vehicles still registered today, so older months are thinned by scrappage and a count would read as sales. Counts wait for true monthly registrations.
Only new or only used vehicles. The site's figures are not yet split that way.
Models. Only the most common models are named, so older months are mostly grouped as other. Models wait for true monthly registrations.
Regions. The register holds each owner's current address, not where the vehicle was first registered.

granularity_options.note: Share, not volume. These are vehicles still registered at the snapshot, so older months are thinned by scrappage and a count would partly measure it. Volume charts wait for true monthly registrations. Group ownership is as at today, not at registration. A rising remainder here is the market fragmenting across groups too small to rank; the concentration chart measures that directly rather than leaving it to be inferred.

presets.question: Which vehicle models lead the market?

presets.note_template: Ranked by vehicles first registered over the trailing {dataset.coverage_trailing.window_months} months. Rank movement compares against the 12 months before. Only the {dataset.model_cap.model.cap} models with the most registrations are named; the rest roll into other.

presets.question: Is the market getting more crowded?
presets.note_template: The combined share of the {measure.top_n} largest brands in each month. Membership is recomputed monthly, so the line reflects concentration rather than the fortunes of a fixed set of brands. A falling line means the largest brands hold less of the market: more brands may be competing, or the same brands may be sharing it more evenly. In the early decades, makes with no match in the brand list count in the total but never take a place, which holds the line down.
